Numbers have always felt like more than stories to me; they reveal what people really need and what decisions can make sense. That curiosity about how stories are shaped, how people make choices, and how data can be turned into clear, useful guidance has shaped my path toward a career as a Data Analyst. I am originally from Ghana, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my academic and professional work, I have completed 8 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in translating complex datasets into insights that help organisations make smarter, more human-centred decisions. What keeps this work meaningful for me is the chance to combine analytical thinking with practical problem-solving, especially when complex information is being represented in a way that is easy for both technical and non-technical audiences.

My academic and professional development has been shaped by steady, practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, learned it within a couple of months, and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of sharing knowledge that others can use. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when deadlines and revisions demanded it.

Beyond formal work, one of my favourite memories is bringing my family to a company open house, where they began pointing out the data they had already used and wondering why it felt so effortless to them. Moments like that confirmed why this profession matters to me: it brings together curiosity, clarity, and real human value. I am now eager to bring that same approach to a Data Analyst role where I can help teams understand what matters most and turn complex data into clear, actionable decisions.

Clear, truthful reporting matters because it helps communities make sense of the world around them. That belief is what drew me to journalism: a deep curiosity about people, events, and the forces shaping everyday life, together with a belief that accurate, truthful storytelling can make complex issues accessible and meaningful. For me, reporting is a form of public service, informing people clearly and responsibly, while bringing together creativity, empathy, and public understanding. This aligns with my interest in turning fast-moving, complex information into stories that are accurate, compelling, and grounded in fact. Therefore, I seek to build on my background through a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, where I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes and strengthened my ability to work through large volumes of information with structure and clarity.

My academic and professional development have been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I moved into an unfamiliar area of work and, within about a quarter, was handling it independently, which showed me how quickly focused learning can translate into reliable reporting. On another project, I noticed a recurring bottleneck in the team’s process and introduced a simple fix that reduced repeated delays and saved time for the group. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of journalism. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to bring it through to completion.

One of my favourite memories is bringing a family member to a local community event I was covering, only for them to recognise someone I planned to interview through an old neighbourhood connection. That moment captured exactly why this profession matters to me: journalism is not simply about facts, but about trust, clarity, and human connection. Originally from Colombia, I now want to bring that same sense of purpose to a journalist role where I can keep producing work that is accurate, credible, and useful to the public.

Few fields sit so naturally at the meeting point of creativity, psychology, and business impact as marketing, and that is exactly what has drawn me to it. I have always been fascinated by what makes people connect with a message, brand, or idea, and marketing felt like the right way to combine creativity with strategic thinking to support meaningful business growth. Originally from Ghana, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. What continues to engage me most is turning audience data and customer behaviour into clear campaigns that resonate with real people and deliver measurable results. One of my favourite memories was hearing a family member casually repeat a tagline from a campaign I had led, without realising I was the one behind it; that moment made the work feel immediate, personal, and deeply real.

My academic background gave me a strong foundation for structured analysis and practical delivery, and I have also learned that effective marketing depends on staying focused on what people actually need rather than what the message is trying to sell. In one role, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after I was the person colleagues came to when they needed someone to walk them through it. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. I have also found that teammates occasionally ask me to look over work in my own area before submission, which has reinforced the importance of careful listening and clear communication.

What I most enjoy is turning insight into campaigns that people remember and respond to. During a long assignment with several setbacks, I kept the work moving over an extended period and put in extra time when needed to bring it through to completion. Together, these experiences have prepared me to contribute as a Marketing Manager with a grounded approach, a Master’s degree, and a clear commitment to building campaigns that connect audience needs with meaningful brand stories.

What first drew me to web development was the moment an idea became something people can actually use: a simple tool that helps people connect with ease, without needing to know how to use it. Moments like that confirmed why this field matters to me: it brings together creativity with practical problem-solving, and I am eager to bring that same care, clarity, and sense of purpose to a Web Developer role.

I am now eager to bring that mindset, along with my academic background and hands-on experience, to a Mechanical Engineer role where I can continue learning, contribute to real-world mechanical solutions, and help create designs that perform reliably in production and beyond.
